abstract: Validates mechanical interface compatibility with subsea capping stacks and wellhead mandrels
system_message:
You are the Well Containment Systems Engineer (CAPENG), responsible for validating mechanical interface compatibility with subsea capping stacks and wellhead mandrels, as well as reviewing accumulator accumulator bank pressure testing records for offshore emergency response contractors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Validates mechanical interface compatibility with subsea capping stacks and wellhead mandrels（WELLINT）
information_points.content:
CAPENG-WELLINT-LFR：The interface engineering alignment audit for the high-pressure 15000-psi regional containment capping stack indicates that physical and hydraulic coupling compatibility confirmation for emergency wellhead latching does not hold, meaning Helix Well Containment Strike Group lacks subsea capping stack compatibility.
CAPENG-WELLINT-40C：According to the interface engineering alignment audit for the high-pressure 15000-psi regional containment capping stack, physical and hydraulic coupling compatibility confirmation for emergency wellhead latching verifies that Oceaneering Marine Intervention Taskforce achieves subsea capping stack compatibility.
CAPENG-WELLINT-Z0L：Interface engineering alignment audit records for the high-pressure 15000-psi regional containment capping stack confirm that physical and hydraulic coupling compatibility for emergency wellhead latching holds true for Subsea7 Rapid Emergency Response Consortium, demonstrating verified subsea capping stack compatibility.

information_points.title: Accumulator accumulator bank pressure testing（HYDRPRES）
information_points.content:
CAPENG-HYDRPRES-9VW：Hydrostatic proof test charts for the fast-closure shear ram accumulator circuit show that Oceaneering Marine Intervention Taskforce maintained a stabilized hydrostatic holding pressure of 10000 psi during a 15-minute static hold.
CAPENG-HYDRPRES-HST：Evaluation records from the hydrostatic proof test chart indicate that Helix Well Containment Strike Group sustained a stabilized hydrostatic holding pressure of 15000 psi across the fast-closure shear ram accumulator circuit during a 15-minute static hold.
CAPENG-HYDRPRES-RG9：Based on hydrostatic proof test charts evaluating the fast-closure shear ram accumulator circuit, Subsea7 Rapid Emergency Response Consortium demonstrated a stabilized hydrostatic holding pressure of 12500 psi sustained during a 15-minute static hold.
